title: Culture Could Be Driving Human Evolution and Turning Us Into Superorganisms
titleZh: 基因退居二线，文化正在重塑人类命运
summary:
提到进化，人们往往会想到达尔文的雀鸟和自然选择。但在《生物科学》期刊上发表文章的研究人员指出，如今真正决定人类进化方向的并不是基因，而是文化。缅因大学生态与环境科学研究员扎卡里·伍德在一份声明中表示：“文化进化的速度远远超过基因进化，两者完全不在一个量级。”如果真如伍德及其合著者蒂莫西·瓦林所说，文化已经取代生物学，成为人类进化的主导力量，那么我们或许正身处一场进化方式的重大转变之中。

来源：发现杂志；作者：Rosie McCall；原文发布时间：2025-09-25 20:00:00

paragraphs.contentEn: Think of evolution, and you might think of Darwin’s finches and natural selection. But according to researchers writing in the journal BioScience, it is not our genes that are determining our current evolutionary journey. It is our culture. “Cultural evolution eats genetic evolution for breakfast,” Zachary Wood, a researcher in ecology and environmental sciences at the University of Maine, said in a statement, “it's not even close.” If — as Wood and his co-author Timothy Waring say — culture has overtaken biology as the predominant evolutionary force in our species, we could be in the midst of an evolutionary transition.
paragraphs.contentZh: 提到进化，人们往往会想到达尔文的雀鸟和自然选择。但在《生物科学》期刊上发表文章的研究人员指出，如今真正决定人类进化方向的并不是基因，而是文化。缅因大学生态与环境科学研究员扎卡里·伍德在一份声明中表示：“文化进化的速度远远超过基因进化，两者完全不在一个量级。”如果真如伍德及其合著者蒂莫西·瓦林所说，文化已经取代生物学，成为人类进化的主导力量，那么我们或许正身处一场进化方式的重大转变之中。

paragraphs.contentEn: Every now and then, a species undergoes a transition that ultimately transforms what it means to be an individual — a very early example being when a single cell becomes a multicellular organism. Wood, Waring, and many scholars in the field of evolutionary biology believe we are in the midst of another transition, one that has the potential to turn us into a “superorganism.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 在进化历程中，物种偶尔会经历某种转型，从而彻底改变个体的存在形态——最早的一个例子是单细胞生物演化为多细胞生物。伍德、瓦林以及进化生物学领域的许多学者相信，人类正处在另一次这样的转型之中，而这一次，我们或许正在演化为一个“超级有机体”。

paragraphs.contentEn: In previous chapters of our evolutionary past, the most fundamental changes to us as a species have been the result of genetics. Think of our larger brain size, which equips us with the capacity to learn and retain complex skills and language, or menopause, which enables women in middle and later age to pass their skills onto younger generations.
paragraphs.contentZh: 在人类进化的过往篇章中，我们作为一个物种最根本的变化，大多都是基因选择的结果。比如，我们的大脑容量逐渐增大，从而具备了学习和掌握复杂技能与语言的能力；又比如更年期的出现，使中老年女性能够将毕生的经验技能传授给年轻一代。

paragraphs.contentEn: The issue with genetic change is that it tends to be slow and gradual. Cultural evolution, in contrast, can occur within the time it takes to pass a piece of legislation. “Human evolution seems to be changing gears,” Waring, an associate professor of economics and sustainability at the University of Maine, said in a press release. “On reviewing the evidence, we find that culture solves problems much more rapidly than genetic evolution. This suggests our species is in the middle of a great evolutionary transition.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 但基因进化的过程往往是缓慢而渐进的。相比之下，文化进化则可以在短时间内发生，有时甚至快到只需一项法案通过的时间。该研究的合著者、缅因大学经济学与可持续发展副教授瓦林在一份新闻稿中指出：“人类的进化似乎正在换挡。综合现有证据来看，文化进化在应对挑战方面的速度远快于基因进化。这意味着，我们这个物种正处在一场重大的进化转型中。”

paragraphs.contentEn: Cultural practices incorporate everything from farming techniques and legal requirements to medical advances. And cultural evolution in and of itself is not new — an early example is the transition to agriculture, which has seen most of the world’s population move from hunter-gatherer societies to permanent settlements. But, Wood and Waring argue, the speed and scale of cultural evolution is ramping up. When we see increases in our life expectancy and improvements in our health, it is less often the result of genes and more likely the product of advancements in healthcare, sanitation systems, and other group-based infrastructure.
paragraphs.contentZh: 文化实践涵盖了从耕作技术、法律制度到医疗进步等方方面面。文化进化本身并不是新现象——早期的一个例子就是人类向农业社会的转变，这一转型让全球大多数人口从狩猎采集走向了永久定居。但伍德和瓦林指出，如今文化进化的速度和规模正在急剧提升。当我们看到人类预期寿命延长、健康状况改善时，其背后更多并不是基因作用，而是医疗进步、公共卫生体系以及其他社会基础设施的发展。

paragraphs.contentEn: Still not convinced? “Ask yourself this: what matters more for your personal life outcomes, the genes you are born with, or the country where you live?” said Waring in the press statement. “Today, your well-being is determined less and less by your personal biology and more and more by the cultural systems that surround you — your community, your nation, your technologies.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 还是觉得难以置信？“你可以问自己一个问题：对你的人生产生更大影响的究竟是什么？是你与生俱来的基因，还是你所处的国家？如今，个人的福祉越来越少地取决于自身的生物条件，而更多地受到周围文化系统的影响——比如你所在的社区、国家，或是你所使用的技术”，瓦林在新闻声明中说道。

paragraphs.contentEn: Evolutionary transition in individuality (ETI) describes the process of a formerly independent organism turning into a component within a larger group. It can refer to individual cells within an organism or ants within a colony. In the case of the latter, the ant colony is a “superorganism” in which the individual ants are so dependent on the group that it essentially functions as its own unit.
paragraphs.contentZh: “个体性进化转型”（ETI）指的是一个曾经独立的有机体逐渐演变为更大群体中的一个组成部分的过程。这一概念既可以用来解释有机体内部的单个细胞，也可以用来说明蚁群中的一只蚂蚁。就后者而言，整个蚁群就是一个“超级有机体”：个体蚂蚁对群体的依赖程度之高，以致整个蚁群实质上作为一个独立的单元在运作。

paragraphs.contentEn: Based on our current trajectory, some scholars believe this is where we are heading. Wood and Waring offer a system for testing the theory and measuring how far along this road we may be. They do not believe we are there yet, but write: “We speculate that, in the long term, culture will continue to grow in influence over human evolution until genes become secondary structures that encode human biological design blueprints but are ultimately governed by culture.”
paragraphs.contentZh: 基于我们目前的发展轨迹，一些学者认为人类正朝着这一方向演进。伍德和瓦林建立了一套体系，用于检验这一理论，并评估人类在此进程中已经到达的阶段。他们并不认为人类已经抵达转型的终点，但在文中写道：“我们推测，从长远来看，文化在人类进化过程中的影响力将不断增强，直到基因退居次要地位，仅作为编码人类生物学设计蓝图的底层结构，而文化则成为主导进化的核心力量。”
